name: Classic Panzanella Salad (Tuscan-Style Tomato-And-Bread Salad)
headnote: J. Kenji Lopez-Alt frames panzanella as a bread salad flavored with vegetables rather than a tomato salad with bread in it, and insists it only works with genuinely good ripe tomatoes. He tested bread four ways - fresh, dried in the oven, stale-but-wrapped, and stale-and-dry - plus the common trick of soaking and squeezing, and concluded that drying is what matters and staling is not: lightly oven-dried fresh bread held its texture best, while wet or merely stale bread turned mushy or leathery. Because drying takes only about 15 minutes in a low oven, the salad needs no day-ahead planning. He also salts and drains the tomatoes for that same 15 minutes to concentrate their flavor, then whisks the drained juice into the vinaigrette with shallot, garlic and a little Dijon, raising the olive oil accordingly so the extra liquid does not break the emulsion.
comment_digest: Reviews are overwhelmingly positive and offer variations more than corrections. The most repeated practical point is that whisking the drained tomato juice into the dressing is the step that makes the recipe, with one cook saying it was exactly what earlier attempts had been missing. Herb substitutions work: cilantro was used successfully and parsley in tabouleh-like quantity is recommended by two people, with oregano suggested untested. Additions people report liking include torn mozzarella or burrata to turn it into a main dish, and green onion in place of shallot. Several note the salting-and-draining trick rescues mediocre off-season supermarket tomatoes and use it on other salads. Bread choice is flexible - flavored bakery loaves, garlic cheddar sourdough and already-stale bread all worked. One unanswered question asks whether the salted tomatoes should be rinsed before going into the salad, as some other Serious Eats recipes direct; another asks whether anchovies and capers are a regional variant.
flags: No corrections to quantities or timings appear in the comments; the hausflip question about whether to rinse the salted tomatoes is left unanswered on the page. Several comments end in 'Read More' and may be truncated.
